title: EDAM project process arguments (*.Args.json)
description: The contract of an EDAM project process-arguments document, as specified by 'EDAM Studio — Understanding Projects' §2.3 (docs/reference/0010 - Edam.Studio.Understanding.Projects.v0.docx), derived from the code model (Edam.Data.AssetConsole.AssetConsoleArgumentsInfo) and the templates this application ships. It is deliberately LENIENT: the specification leaves InspectArguments and ElementTransform as TBD, its own InspectArguments values are strings, and the shipped templates carry only a subset of the sections — so a document that runs today must validate today. Unknown properties are tolerated here and reported by the validator (strictly, when asked).

@context.description: Step 1 — the JSON vocabulary. 'Always include the above at the top of the file.'

Domain.description: Step 2 — the asset domain. The application looks for DomainId when an arguments file is selected and adds the domain to the EDAM database when it is not there yet.

Namespace.description: Step 3 — the asset URI, its prefix and its root element.

Project.description: Step 4 — the project and its version. 'The name must be the same as the Project folder' — a rule no JSON schema can check, so the validator checks it against the project it was given.

Process.description: Step 5 — the process to execute. ProcedureName is the procedure the runner invokes; its valid values are the enumerator values of Edam.Data.AssetConsole.AssetConsoleProcedure (a conformance check keeps this list equal to the code's).

UriList.description: Step 7 — where the input file(s) are, relative to the project folder. Several files compose one set of data elements.

items.description: A project-relative reference such as './Archive/x.xlsx' — never an absolute or drive path.

InspectArguments.description: Step 8 — how to inspect the artifacts. TBD in the specification, and its own values are strings ('1'), so this is deliberately unconstrained.

ConnectionString.description: Step 9 — the database connection string, when the procedure involves a database.

ElementTransform.description: Step 9 — 'will be documented later': deliberately unconstrained.

TextMapFilePath.description: Step 9 — the text-map document that guides language mapping and traversal.
